change_summary: Ran a fixed-snapshot runtime-only monkeypatch of `portfolio_engine.size_signals()` that left entries, exits, ranking order, and LLM scope unchanged, but applied an extra same-day risk multiplier only to `breakout_long` signals whose `trade_quality_score` was below the best same-day `trend_long` TQS. Screened multipliers `0.75x`, `0.5x`, `0.25x`, and `0.0x` across the accepted three-window A+B snapshot stack.
component: experiment-only monkeypatch of `quant/portfolio_engine.py` (rolled back; no repo trading logic changed)

delta_metrics.best_secondary_note: 0.75x was the least bad screened multiplier, but it still regressed expected_value_score in all three windows versus the accepted baseline.
delta_metrics.note: The aggressive `0.0x` version improved the latest strong window, but it clearly failed the multi-window gate by regressing both comparison eras. The milder multipliers also regressed the north-star metric across a majority of windows. Same-day trend-vs-breakout TQS competition is therefore not the missing allocation mechanism.

hypothesis: If current breakout instability is mainly a same-day cross-strategy capital-allocation problem, then `breakout_long` candidates that are outscored by at least one same-day `trend_long` candidate should be de-risked rather than funded at full size. A same-day TQS-relative haircut could preserve the latest strong window while shifting heat toward the more persistent trend sleeve in weaker eras.
next_retry_requires: Do not retry another breakout-vs-trend same-day TQS competition haircut without a genuinely new context source beyond relative pre-entry score ordering
Treat breakout weakness as more than a same-day heat-allocation problem; the missing edge is not simply 'trend deserved the slot more'
If breakout-health work continues, start from a richer context source than same-day score competition, such as a new event/state variable or a narrower repeatedly observed cohort
notes: No repository trading logic was changed for this experiment. The rule was evaluated via an experiment-only monkeypatch so the failure could be logged without leaving dead code behind.

selector.context: same-day signal set contains at least one trend_long candidate
selector.relative_rule: breakout trade_quality_score < max same-day trend_long trade_quality_score

rejection_reason: Rejected on Gate 4 multi-window stability. A same-day relative-TQS haircut on breakout candidates did not improve the expected_value_score in a majority of windows; every mild version regressed all three windows, and the only primary-window winner (`0.0x`) clearly damaged the weak comparison eras.
